core.title: My NotebookLM notebook
core.why: Your own MuleSoft notebook. Use it to ask questions about the study guide and sources, get audio overviews, and check answers after each quiz.

core.title: Anypoint Platform Development: Fundamentals (Mule 4)
core.why: The official self-paced course the exam is built on. Its labs (American Flights API) cover every section. Finishing it has come with free exam attempts; confirm the current offer on the course page.

core.title: Official exam guide
core.why: The list of objectives per section, the format (60 questions, 120 minutes, 70% to pass) and the release the questions follow. Re-read it the day you book.

core.title: Mule 4 error handling docs
core.why: Source for On Error Propagate vs Continue, error types, the error object and error mapping. The exam's trickiest trace-the-flow questions come from here.

core.title: DataWeave 2.0 docs and Playground
core.why: Core functions, selectors and types. Drill in the Playground until you can write map, filter, groupBy, pluck and reduce without looking.

core.title: Mule event, flows and scopes docs
core.why: What payload, attributes and vars hold after each processor, and how flows, subflows, For Each, Scatter-Gather and Batch change them.

resources.title: Anypoint Platform free trial (30 days, start it on Day 1 of hands-on work)
API Manager: Autodiscovery, SLA tiers, client apps
Trailhead: MuleSoft Developer maintenance (Winter '26), shows what changed recently

avoid.name: Brain dumps and "actual exam questions" sites
avoid.reason: Answers are often wrong, and using them breaks the certification agreement. Practice with your own questions and the course quizzes.

avoid.name: Mule 3 material
avoid.reason: Mule 3 used MEL and inbound/outbound properties. The exam is Mule 4 only: DataWeave everywhere, attributes instead of properties.
